Book Name: The Magic of Thinking Big
Chapter 3: “Build confidence and destroy fear”

## LangGraph for Stateful Multi-Agent RAG

LangGraph lets developers build graphs of specialized nodes that share a typed
state. Conditional edges can route execution based on intermediate results.
Cycles enable recovery loops such as re-retrieving when relevance is low, or
regenerating when hallucinations are detected.

## Query Types in Research Assistants

Research questions are often classified as:
- Factual: a single fact can answer the question.
- Multi-hop: information must be combined across passages.
- Comparative: two or more entities or concepts are compared.
- Unanswerable: the corpus does not contain enough information.

## Multi-Query Retrieval

After reading the chapter “Build confidence and destroy fear”, I understood that fear can stop us from doing things even when we are capable of doing them. The chapter explains that confidence is not something that we automatically have from birth. It develops slowly when we face situations, take action and learn from our experiences. I also understood that thinking too much about a fearful situation can make the fear even bigger. Instead of avoiding something because I am afraid, I should first understand what exactly I am afraid of and then do something about it. The chapter also talks about how our past experiences affect our confidence. If I keep remembering only the times when I failed, I will naturally feel less confident. So, I should also remember the things that I have done well.

. The problem was not that I did not have an idea. I was simply afraid that it might not be good enough. Looking back, I feel that even if my idea had been rejected, it would not have been a big problem. At least I would have gained the experience of putting my thoughts forward. That incident made me realize how easily fear of other people's opinions can stop me from taking a simple step.
